blocks.text: "Rasulullaah ﷺ's speech was crisp, with every letter distinctly pronounced."[^1]
Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke anything (of marked importance), he would repeat it thrice and whenever he approached a gathering, he would greet thrice."[^2]

Hadhrat Thumamah bin Anas narrates that whenever Hadhrat Anas (RA) spoke (something of importance), he repeated himself thrice and would say that when Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with Salaam (to seek permission to enter a home), he did so thrice[^3] and when he spoke (something of great importance), he would repeat it thrice.[^4] Hadhrat Anas (RA) also reported that when Rasulullaah ﷺ spoke, he would repeat himself thrice so that people could understand what he was saying."[^5]

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said, "I have been sent with concise yet comprehensive speech and have been assisted with awe. When I was sleeping once, the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand."[^6]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) reports, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down to talk, he would often look towards the sky (in anticipation of revelation)."[^7]
Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) Regrets the Many Questions he Posed to Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "Even when speaking to the worst of people, Rasulullaah ﷺ would turn his full attention to the person so that (they would feel special and) their hearts would be won over. When speaking to me, Rasulullaah ﷺ also turned his full attention towards me until I eventually felt that I was the best of all the Sahabah (RA). 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I once asked, 'Am I better or Abu Bakr?' 'Abu Bakr,' came the reply. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I asked further, 'Am I better or Umar?' When Rasulullaah ﷺ replied that Umar was better, I pursued the enquiry saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Am I better or Uthmaan?' 'Uthmaan,' he replied. After asking Rasulullaah ﷺ and after he had been truthful to me, I wished that I had never asked him these questions."[^8]
The Smiling and Laughing of Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "I have never seen Rasulullaah ﷺ laugh so much
Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted once when first seeking permission to enter, thereafter a second time when entering and finally a third time when leaving.
Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted by Abu Dawood in his Adab. The above narrations have been quoted from Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.40,41).
Tirmidhi in his Shamaa'il (Pg.25). Tabraani has reported a similar narration but Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.15) has commented on the chain of narrators.
